Hello voat, i'm new to building gamming PC's and i have a budget of around 1200 CAD$ where can i get the best PC parts for my money or complete computer I can create with that budget?

I have built a bunch of rigs for my friends at $1000 or lower. One of the best things about PCs is you can potentially skimp on something you want and upgrade later.

Personally I always use Newegg.com. Iv'e had problems with purchases in the past and their customer service has always been fantastic. You can even create a public list of all the parts you want and post that mock-up for feedback.

I recently bought a PC from NewEgg that was a complete dud. It took a few weeks but they refunded me 100% of my purchase price PLUS the $60 I was charged to get a "Free game". I was sure they were going to try to keep that since it was a digital code but they refunded that too.

I haven't bought a prebuilt in years, so I can't comment about the dud, but its good to know that their customer service took care of you,

I had a Thrust-master Warthog HoTAS fail on me after having it for 2 months and they replaced it for me. I'll be a loyal customer for life,

My advice is take your time and watch sales at Newegg and amazon. Stuff like the case and power supply dont outdate as soon as you buy them. Research motherboards and figure out what you can live with out and what you absolutely need. Once you do that dont fall into the hype and stick with the plan

http://www.pcpartpicker.com

It automatically compares prices from all the major online stores (newegg, amazon, tigerdirect, etc.), it also lets you assemble a full build online and lets you narrow down hardware by what is compatible with the hardware you have already selected.

As for advice, I have a few tips.

  1. Invest in a heavy power supply, way more than you need right now. Like, at least 1000w. This is a great way of future proofing your computer and allowing yourself room for upgrades down the line. Get a modular one if you care about cable clutter.

  2. Get the highest capacity RAM you can find so you have the least amount of occupied slots. So instead of buying 2-2GB sticks, try to find a 4GB single stick. This frees up a slot for future upgrades.

  3. If you're concerned about speed or do a lot of gaming, consider investing in an SSD. You'll need a regular hard drive for storage since SSD's are a little too expensive to buy in high capacities right now, but installing your operating system and games on an SSD and storing all your files like movies and such on a regular hard drive will dramatically boost your loading speeds.

  4. Don't fall for "gaming" hardware. It's usually bullshit marketing and it's usually going to cost you more. Find hardware that is well reviewed (check out the charts on http://www.tomshardware.com to see a bunch of different comparisons on all the latest hardware) and is capable of doing what you want.

The biggest tip I can give is to establish exactly what you want out of this computer and find hardware to match. If you want to game, make sure you invest in a decent graphics card. If you do video editing or modeling or anything like that, make sure you get dickloads of ram. If you're just going to use it for music and movies or want to eventually connect other devices in your house to it to stream, invest in lots of storage.

Good luck, I love seeing people wanting to build their own computers. If you have any questions feel free to ask, I've been doing this for a while now and I can probably help.

There is almost no configuration and average user will ever run across that 1000w won't handle just fine, and it allows for almost unlimited room for growth, whether it be hardware, peripherals, cooling, accessories, or mods. I am the kind of person that enjoys buying something for life. If I can buy it once and never have to buy it again, I'm going to. And since power supply technology hasn't really advanced much and probably won't aside from minute efficiency increases, there's really no reason not to buy the best one you can afford, and a 1000w will follow you through multiple builds if you buy a good one.

Most motherboards come with four RAM slots so expanding is not a problem in the first place, but above everything else RAM isn't something that you add to every year or even five. Last Sunday, I had a piece of birthday cake and some ice cream. Today, I had rice with lunch and got frozen yoghurt afterward. I've been behaving perfectly other than that. My question is whether I'm shooting myself in the foot by getting fat people food once a week. Any experiences/suggestions?
How much cheating can you get away with without ruining the diet?

It depends on what you mean by "ruining the diet," doesn't it? If you want to remain in ketosis all the time, then that plan is "ruined" by a slice of birthday cake, for sure. But if you want to keep your insulin down in general, it might not be so bad to have a carb day once a week. If you go that route, you're not doing keto, but a form of carb cycling, I suppose.

It ultimately depends on how your body handles it, though. Some people need to be much more strict than others. Whether you're younger or older, male or female (and if female, premenopausal or postmenopausal), whether you have had a lifetime of building up insulin resistance — these are all factors (so I've heard) that can affect how strict you need to be to get results.

Right now, I allow myself carbs on the weekends, usually simple things like yogurt and berries. (I also drop my insulin through both intermittent and prolonged fasting.) This works well for me, but might not for others. Give your idea a shot and see how it goes.

It will prolong or prevent actual fat adaptation. That requires relatively strict, cheat-free, eating for a month or longer. That means you'll struggle more with exercise on your non-cheat days. Those who are particularly athletic report serious performance deficits and recovery issues for several weeks. I've seen someone say as long as three months in their experience. Of course, it all depends on how well your body handles carbs. Some people can have cheats and still reach fat adaptation without issue.

As for whether or not you can still lose weight cheating once a week, you probably can. There are some people who aren't able to, but most people will get enough benefit from the overall carb-reduction to lose weight. You may struggle more with cravings and water-weight fluctuations than other people who aren't cheating weekly.

Hmm it depends what you are trying to do. The nice thing about Ketosis is that you can do in and out. Going out isn't ideal and costs you fat adaptation, but it does not ruin the losses so far. No way.
Not sure about the health and ketosis effects, but I used to eat one oreo a day to keep my sugar addiction in check. Don't need to now though, and was always in ketosis before.

It entirely depends on how athletic you are and how you time the carbs. If you're a long-distance runner/rower and you eat an extra 20-30g of carb on the days you do long runs (8+ miles) it probably isn't going to knock you out of keto, as most of the carbs go right into glycogen or just get burned. This is how TKD (targeted ketogenic diet) or CKD (cyclical ketogenic diet) work. In TKD you eat carbs before exercise, on CKD you "carb up" once a week. I don't do either; I want to control my body burning fat or glycogen based on my exertion, not via my diet. I also don't do CKD as carby foods are no longer appealing to me as "food".

How many of you use FreeBSD for destkop usage

Not as my daily driver, but I do have two desktops that utilize FreeBSD. One is a striaght-up build with Gnome and Kodi, and the other is PCBSD, which is based on FreeBSD, running a customized Openbox environment. The advantages are, respectively: a very streamlined build for an HTPC on extremely old hardware that needs ahem no distractions, and, in the case of PCBSD, everything I could ever want in BSD user land at my fingertips, with the general guarantee that, as long as I stay in the PCBSD installation sandbox, it will play well and give me no problems, allowing me to focus on customizing the UI without having to piddle with maintaining source packages and such.
